clue.text: Captain Nemo and I fighting to get freedom for slaves?

indicators.note: people fighting are thrown into disorder, so these letters are scrambled into a new order

explanation.surface: Jules Verne's submarine captain and the speaker battle to liberate the enslaved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fighting' tells you to rearrange the letters of CAPTAIN NEMO and I; 'and' only joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: Emancipation is the legal release of enslaved people, as in Lincoln's 1863 proclamation, so it is their freedom.

clue.text: Auntie, perhaps, runs out in euphoria

indicators.note: out means the runs are taken away from the word for a family member

parts.note: an aunt is an example of a relation
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: An aunt rushes out, overjoyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' removes R (runs) from RELATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Elation is great happiness and excitement, much the same as euphoria.

clue.text: A prize for wasting?

parts.note: a trophy is a prize such as a cup

explanation.surface: Asks whether a prize is being awarded for wasting time.
explanation.definitionFit: Atrophy is the wasting away of a muscle or organ through disuse or disease.

clue.text: City has Mayor's first bird flying in enclosure

indicators.note: in tells you to place those letters inside the word for an enclosure

parts.note: a cage is an enclosure for animals

indicators.note: first means only the opening letter of Mayor's is taken
flying suggests the letters are tossed about and rearranged

explanation.surface: A city whose mayor's prize bird escapes and flutters around an aviary.
explanation.walkthrough: M (Mayor's first) plus BRID (from 'bird', 'flying') go 'in' CAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Cambridge is a university city in eastern England.

clue.text: Sat and asked a question?

definitions.meaning: sat for a portrait or photograph
to pose a question is to ask it

explanation.surface: Someone sat down and raised a query.
explanation.definitionFit: A model posed for an artist; a speaker posed a question, putting it forward.

clue.text: Unusual niche in training college at first for practical skill

indicators.note: in tells you to put the rearranged letters inside the two initials
at first means only the opening letters of training college are used
unusual signals the letters of niche are set out in an odd new order

explanation.surface: An odd specialism found at a training college, offered for hands-on ability.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusual' rearranges NICHE to ECHNI, which goes 'in' TC, the first letters of 'training college'.
explanation.definitionFit: Technic is a less common form of technique, meaning skill in carrying out a task.

clue.text: Religious group with Oedipus complex

indicators.note: complex means intricate or tangled, so the letters of the name are mixed up

explanation.surface: A sect obsessed with the Oedipus complex of Freudian psychology.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complex' completes the Freudian phrase in the surface but tells you to rearrange OEDIPUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Opus Dei is a Catholic institution of laypeople and priests founded in Spain in 1928.

clue.text: You may need these when arranging vacation in Santa Cruz, initially

indicators.note: arranging means putting things in a new order, so the letters are rearranged
initially means the opening letters of Santa and Cruz are taken

explanation.surface: Planning a holiday in Santa Cruz may mean getting the right jabs first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranging' rearranges VACATION, IN and SC, the opening letters of 'Santa Cruz' ('initially').
explanation.definitionFit: Travellers to some regions are required or advised to have injections against diseases there.

clue.text: A horse and sheep? One's above and below!

parts.note: a nag is an old or worn-out horse
a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: A farmyard pairing of a horse and a sheep, then a cheeky remark about what sits on top and underneath.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is self-referential: the clue directly above (1 Across) and the one directly below (9 Across) both use this device.
explanation.definitionFit: Both neighbouring clues work by rearranging letters, so each is an example of this kind of wordplay.

clue.text: Gucci (topless) with bus transported she-devils

indicators.note: transported means carried away into a new arrangement, so the combined letters are rearranged
being topless means losing the top, the first letter of the word Gucci

explanation.surface: Designer Gucci clothing, worn topless, carried on a bus by female demons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' takes the G from GUCCI, leaving UCCI; 'transported' then rearranges UCCI with BUS.
explanation.definitionFit: A succubus is a female demon of folklore said to seduce sleeping men; the plural is succubi.

clue.text: Edible? It's gin, stupid — it can't be eaten!

indicators.note: stupid means senseless or muddled, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone protests that a gin-soaked dish is not edible at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stupid' tells you to rearrange EDIBLE, IT'S and GIN; the clue claims one thing is edible and then says the opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: Indigestible food cannot be properly digested, so it is not fit to eat.

clue.text: Fit a wood-processing machine?

definitions.meaning: lively and cheerful, in good health
a machine that turns branches and logs into wood chips

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a tool for processing timber is suitable.
explanation.definitionFit: Chipper is informal for cheerful and in good shape; the machine sense comes from chipping wood.

clue.text: Brown, put back in act, stripped

indicators.note: in tells you to place the reversed colour inside the word for act

parts.note: a deed is an act

indicators.note: put back means the colour word is reversed, its letters running the other way

parts.note: dun is a dull greyish-brown colour

explanation.surface: Someone surnamed Brown, returned to a theatre act, has been stripped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brown' reads like a surname but gives the colour DUN; 'put back' turns it into NUD, which goes 'in' DEED.
explanation.definitionFit: Denuded means laid bare, with its covering removed, which is what stripped describes.

clue.text: Childminder getting one's goat?

definitions.meaning: a ... goat is a female goat, so a ... is one kind of goat

explanation.surface: A babysitter is being irritated, as in getting someone's goat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting one's goat' is an idiom for annoying someone, but here 'getting' is only a link and 'one's goat?' asks for a type of goat.
explanation.definitionFit: A nanny looks after a family's children; separately, a female goat is called a nanny goat.

clue.text: Showing the removal of old Scots people?

definitions.meaning: portraying or representing in a picture

definitions.text: the removal of old Scots people?
definitions.meaning: the Picts were an ancient people of Scotland

explanation.surface: A display about clearing out the ancient inhabitants of Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer as DE- (removal) + PICT + -ING, a playful invented verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To depict is to portray or represent, so depicting is showing something in art or words.

clue.text: Bill takes it? Yes, primarily for those who will come after

parts.note: a bill is a poster stuck up in public

indicators.note: primarily means only the first letter of Yes is used

explanation.surface: Someone named Bill accepts something and agrees, thinking of future generations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' reads like a name but means a poster; 'takes' joins it to IT, then Y from 'Yes'.
explanation.definitionFit: Posterity means all future generations, the people who live after us.

clue.text: Lacking aesthetic judgement in how food may appear after Covid

definitions.meaning: showing poor taste in style or decoration

definitions.text: how food may appear after Covid
definitions.meaning: Covid often caused a loss of taste

explanation.surface: A complaint about poor style, linked to the loss of flavour that followed a Covid infection.
explanation.definitionFit: Tasteless covers both vulgar or unrefined style and food that has no flavour.

clue.text: Son ends up going off to stay for a while

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son, as in family trees

indicators.note: going off means going bad or going astray, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A son's visit finishes with him leaving after a short stay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going off' signals the anagram; 'stay' is the verb meaning to halt or defer, not to remain.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay a sentence or a process is to halt it temporarily, exactly what suspending it does.

clue.text: Fetes I announce in periodical? Quite the opposite!

indicators.note: in would mean the phrase is inside the periodical, the next words reverse that
quite the opposite flips the sense: the periodical word lies inside the phrase

parts.note: the letters run across the three words

explanation.surface: An organiser plans to advertise local fairs in a magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: Read plainly, 'in periodical' says the phrase is inside the answer; 'Quite the opposite!' says the answer is inside fETES I ANnounce. 'periodical' is an adjective here, not a magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: Etesian winds blow at regular times each year in the Mediterranean, so etesian means periodic or annual.

clue.text: The late archbishop's skirts?

definitions.meaning: Desmond Tutu, archbishop of Cape Town, died in 2021
the short stiff skirts worn by ballerinas

explanation.surface: A question about the clothing of the late archbishop.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive TUTU'S is read without its apostrophe as the plural of tutu.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutu is a ballet dancer's layered net skirt, so tutus are skirts.

clue.text: Fabric in Welsh river with letter from Greece pinned to it

indicators.note: pinned to it means the Greek letter is attached after the river

parts.note: the Taff is the river that flows through Cardiff in Wales
eta is the seventh letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A cloth spotted in a Welsh river, with a note from Greece attached.
explanation.walkthrough: The Taff is a river in south Wales running through Cardiff.
explanation.definitionFit: Taffeta is a crisp, lustrous woven fabric, often of silk.

clue.text: Town lady, short of oxygen, getting agitated in Parliament

indicators.note: getting agitated means stirred up, so the remaining letters are shaken into a new order
short of means lacking, so the oxygen symbol is removed from these words

parts.note: O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A local woman, out of breath, grows flustered in the debating chamber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short of' removes O from TOWN LADY, leaving TWNLADY, which 'getting agitated' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Tynwald is the parliament of the Isle of Man, said to be the oldest continuous one in the world.

clue.text: Former pupil with view that's disgusting

parts.note: OB is old boy, a former pupil of a school
a scene is a view or landscape

explanation.surface: An old school graduate with an outlook that others find repellent.
explanation.walkthrough: OB, for 'old boy', is standard British usage for a school's former pupil.
explanation.definitionFit: Obscene describes something offensive or repugnant, a close synonym of disgusting.

clue.text: Emile concocted a fragrant substance

indicators.note: concocted means mixed up from ingredients, so the letters of the name are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man called Emile has mixed up a perfume.
explanation.definitionFit: Elemi is a fragrant resin from tropical trees, used in varnishes and perfumes.

clue.text: Old Turkish official fed fine cooking

indicators.note: cooking the books means falsifying them, so the letters here are tampered with and rearranged

explanation.surface: An Ottoman dignitary was given a good meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooking' tells you to rearrange the letters of FED and FINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Effendi was a title of respect for an official or educated man in the Ottoman Empire.

clue.text: Sister I left, somewhat lacking in creativity

indicators.note: somewhat means only part of the phrase is used, so the answer sits inside those words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A nun who leaves the convent confesses she was rather short of imagination.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took only 'creativity' as the definition, but the answer means 'lacking in creativity'; the indicator is 'somewhat' alone. The answer sits in siSTER I LEft.
explanation.definitionFit: Sterile can mean unproductive or uninspired, producing no new ideas.

clue.text: I shout, absorbing loud echo returning in part of glacier

indicators.note: absorbing means taking something in, so the shout holds the other letters

parts.note: to call is to shout

indicators.note: returning means the letters for loud and echo come back in the reverse order

parts.note: F is forte, the musical direction for loud
Echo is E in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A climber yells and hears the echo bouncing back across the glacier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns FE into EF, which goes inside CALL, after I.
explanation.definitionFit: An icefall is a steep, broken stretch of a glacier, like a frozen waterfall.

clue.text: Doctor and city tried to obtain proof of citizenship

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so these letters are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: A physician and a city council try to get documents proving nationality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a person but is a verb telling you to rearrange AND CITY TRIED.
explanation.definitionFit: An identity card is an official document confirming who someone is and their nationality.
